data.cultural_impact: Sugrivpal is a significant cultural figure in Indian mythology, particularly in the context of the Ramayana. He is known for his unwavering loyalty to Sita, the maiden wife of Lord Rama, and his instrumental role in aiding Rama in rescuing Sita from the demon king Ravana. Sugrivpal's determination and courage have made him a revered figure in Indian folklore and literature, and his story continues to be a source of inspiration and moral guidance for countless individuals.
data.spiritual_significance: Sugrivpal represents the power of loyalty and selflessness, two virtues that are highly valued in Hindu spirituality. His unwavering commitment to Sita, even when she was unknowingly in the possession of his sworn enemy, Ravana, demonstrates the importance of remaining true to one's moral values and spiritual principles, no matter the circumstances. Moreover, Sugrivpal's ultimate sacrifice in volunteering to be a spy in Ravana's court in order to aid Rama in rescuing Sita, illustrates the selfless act of placing others' needs above one's own. Overall, Sugrivpal serves as an embodiment of the Hindu spiritual values of sacrifice, loyalty, and selflessness.

historical_references.reference: Sugriva was a Vanar king who ruled over the monkey kingdom Kishkindha in the Indian subcontinent. He was the brother of Vali and the father of Angada. Sugriva's throne was usurped by his brother Vali, and he was forced to flee the kingdom. Vali was eventually killed by Rama, and Sugriva regained his throne with the help of Rama and Hanuman. This event is described in the Indian epic Ramayana, believed to have been composed between 4th and 1st centuries BCE.
historical_references.context: Ramayana, brother of Vali, usurped throne, regained with help from Rama and Hanuman

historical_references.reference: Sugriva was also mentioned in various Jain and Buddhist texts as a powerful king and a great warrior. In Jain texts, Sugriva is described as a Yaksha king and a patron of Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara. In Buddhist texts, Sugriva is mentioned as a supporter of the Buddha and an ally of the monkey king Sihanaka. These texts date back to the 3rd century BCE.
historical_references.context: Jain and Buddhist texts, powerful king, patron of Mahavira, ally of Sihanaka
